kjv.text: And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

bsb.text: So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.

web.text: Then the LORD’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”

flow.text: Henry shows how Isaiah's promise of return to Zion points to two kinds of joy: the comfort God gives his people now, and the endless joy waiting for them in heaven.

Here is good news for the citizens of Zion, rest to the weary: *The ransomed of the Lord,* who therefore ought to follow him wherever he goes (Re 14:4), *shall return and come to Zion,* 1. To serve and worship God in the church militant: they shall deliver themselves out of Babylon (Zec 2:7), shall *ask the way to Zion* (Jer 50:5), and shall *find the way* Isa 52:12.
The ransomed leave their captivity and come back to worship God, singing as they go because their sorrow has turned to praise.

When they shall *enter into the joy of their Lord* it shall be what the joys of this world never could be *everlasting joy,* without mixture, interruption, or period. It shall not only fill their hearts, to their own perfect and perpetual satisfaction, but it shall be *upon their heads,* as an ornament of grace and a crown of glory, as a garland worn in token of victory.
That joy in heaven will be perfect and visible, worn like a crown, nothing like the mixed and hidden joys we know on earth.
They shall then obtain the joy and gladness which they could never expect on this side heaven; *and sorrow and sighing shall flee away* for ever, as the shadows of the night before the rising sun.

morning.say: Carry with you today the thought that your present sorrows point toward the everlasting joy that waits.
morning.phrase: sorrow and sighing shall flee away for ever

leads.kjv: For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem: thou shalt weep no more: he will be very gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee.
And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken it.
